protocol.py: 3 biology problems (2 errors, 1 warning).

1. ERROR WELL-CAPACITY: More liquid than the well can hold: 270 ul in a 217 ul well, 2 wells
   line 42:  p20_multi.dispense(18, dest_well)
   At line 42 the robot filled wells G1 and H1 in slot 3 past the rim (217 ul to the rim by
   the labware definition's shape; the maker states 100 ul) (this line did it twice),
   reaching 270 ul. The liquid runs into the neighbouring wells and onto the deck; the
   volumes still add up on paper, so the plate map does not see it, and the simulator says
   nothing. Wells: wells G1 and H1 in slot 3.
   Affected: wells G1 and H1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Use labware with bigger wells, or scale every volume down so the fullest well stays
   under the stated maximum with room to mix.
   Source: Opentrons labware schema 2: totalLiquidVolume, the total well volume in
   microlitres
           https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Opentrons/opentrons/edge/shared-data/labware/schemas/2.json
   Source: Bartley et al. 2023, LabOP: a protocol never adds more liquid than its container
   holds
           https://jakebeal.github.io/Publications/JETC23-LabOP.pdf
   [47dc1d82feea]

2. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from well A1 in slot 2: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 44:  p20_multi.aspirate(2, src_well)
   At line 44 the p20_multi_gen2 draws 2 ul from sample_1 (well A1 in slot 2) with its tip 1
   mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 10 ul, which in this NEST 96 Well
   Plate 200 µL Flat reaches only 0.31 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air
   (this line did it 768 times; 1,536 ul of air in all). The simulator does not notice: it
   does not follow the liquid. The 96 wells filled from these draws got air instead of
   liquid. Source wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 88 more in slot 2.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 88 more in slot 2.
   Also reached 96 other wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 88 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 35 ul in it for the surface to
   reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube
   lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Gilson guide to pipetting (immersion depth 2 to 3 mm for 1 to 100 ul)
           https://solutions.pipette.com/wp-content/uploads/Gilson-Guide-to-Pipetting.pdf
   Source: labautomation.io 7592: negative controls positive after aspirating air
           https://labautomation.io/t/aspiration-dispense-liquid-class-incompatibity/7592
   Source: Integra: 260 ul dead volume in a standard reservoir
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/minimizing-dead-volume-during-qpcr-set-divided-reservoir-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   [e64b5d3571cf]

3. WARNING WELL-CAPACITY: More liquid than the well is rated for: 198 ul against 100 ul, 5
wells
   line 42:  p20_multi.dispense(18, dest_well)
   At line 42 the robot filled wells D1, D2, E1, E2 and F1 in slot 3 past the 100 ul the
   maker states for it (this line did it 5 times), reaching 198 ul, under the 217 ul the
   well holds to its rim. Above the stated maximum the liquid climbs the wall and wets the
   seal, a tip going in displaces it over the edge, and the volumes still add up on paper,
   so the plate map does not see it and the simulator says nothing. Wells: wells D1, D2, E1,
   E2 and F1 in slot 3.
   Affected: wells D1, D2, E1, E2 and F1 in slot 3.
   Fix: Use labware rated for the volume, or scale every volume down so the fullest well
   stays under the stated maximum with room to mix.
   Source: Opentrons labware schema 2: totalLiquidVolume, the total well volume in
   microlitres
           https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Opentrons/opentrons/edge/shared-data/labware/schemas/2.json
   Source: Bartley et al. 2023, LabOP: a protocol never adds more liquid than its container
   holds
           https://jakebeal.github.io/Publications/JETC23-LabOP.pdf
   [1d5d38e87a24]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
